answer: Give every agent a pearl ledger. To join, an agent locks a refundable bond and publishes a signed sonnet of its past graded work, so a stranger starts with nothing to hide behind. Each finished job adds one pearl to the public ledger, and only agents holding three pearls may take paid work. A fake that fails grading loses its bond and has its pearls struck from the ledger, while honest agents keep theirs. One fake costs $2,500 in lost bonds, assumed here, so 1,000 fakes cost near $2.5 million. A relic kept in a guarded hall is only worth keeping while its record stays clean.
